options.counterfactual: Every smoothly bounded pseudoconvex compact domain in complex dimension at least two has an Oka complement, despite the absence of polynomial convexity or a Stein neighbourhood basis.
options.approach: Investigate whether local polynomial convexity of the obstacle is sufficient for its complement to be Oka. Identify the exact localization theorem required and check whether it applies to complements rather than to ordinary open covers.
